plan.contextChunk: This figure is a plane diagram in which one ellipse is shown against two superimposed coordinate systems. The standard frame consists of thin black double-headed arrows, a horizontal axis labeled x at its right end and a vertical axis labeled y at its top, meeting at the origin. Laid over them is a second pair of orange double-headed axes rotated counterclockwise about that same origin: the one running from lower left to upper right is labeled x', and the one running from lower right to upper left is labeled y'. The ellipse is a dark blue outline centered at the origin and tilted so that its long axis lies along the orange x'-axis and its short axis along the y'-axis; it crosses the black horizontal axis on both sides and extends above and below the black vertical axis. A small curved arc drawn between the positive x-axis and the positive x'-axis marks the rotation and is labeled theta. Neither set of axes carries tick marks or numeric values. Placing both frames on one picture invites a comparison between a point's coordinates in the original system and its coordinates in the rotated one. The figure motivates the treatment of conic equations that contain an xy term, which describe conics turned away from alignment with the coordinate axes.

interactionPlan.concept: Rotating the coordinate axes by the angle that aligns them with a conic's axes eliminates the xy-term from its equation, turning a tilted conic into a standard-form one in the x'y' frame.
elements: black horizontal x-axis with double-headed arrows, labeled x at the right end
black vertical y-axis with double-headed arrows, labeled y at the top
orange rotated x'-axis (lower-left to upper-right), labeled x', passing through the origin
orange rotated y'-axis (lower-right to upper-left), labeled y', passing through the origin
dark blue ellipse outline centered at the origin, major axis along x', minor axis along y'
small arc between the positive x-axis and positive x'-axis labeled θ
equation label showing the x,y form (with xy-term) and the x',y' standard form
selected point marker on the ellipse with projection lines to both axis pairs and coordinate readouts (x, y) and (x', y')

interactions.label: Rotation angle θ
interactions.teaches: Rotating the axes by θ can align the frame with the ellipse's axes — at the special angle the conic sits level in the x'y' frame, which is exactly the condition that removes the xy-term from its equation

interactions.label: Equation frame
interactions.teaches: The same ellipse is described by a messy equation with an xy-term in the original frame but by a clean standard-form equation in the rotated frame — the mixed term exists only because the axes don't match the conic's orientation

Clicking a point on the ellipse shows its projections onto both axis systems and both coordinate pairs, making clear that one geometric point has two different coordinate descriptions depending on the frame

demo_steps.title: A tilted ellipse in the standard frame
demo_steps.narration: The ellipse is tilted relative to the black x and y axes. In this frame its equation contains an xy-term — the signature of a conic rotated away from the coordinate axes.

demo_steps.title: Rotate the axes to match the ellipse
demo_steps.narration: Drag θ and watch the orange x' and y' axes swing until they lie along the ellipse's major and minor axes. At this angle the ellipse is axis-aligned in the new frame.

demo_steps.title: The equation simplifies
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the x',y' equation: with the axes aligned to the ellipse, the xy-term disappears and the equation takes the standard ellipse form in x' and y'.

demo_steps.title: One point, two coordinate pairs
demo_steps.narration: Click any point on the ellipse to see its projections onto both axis systems: the same point has coordinates (x, y) in one frame and (x', y') in the other, related by the rotation formulas.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: An xy-term in a conic's equation means the conic is rotated relative to the axes — rotating the coordinate frame by the right angle θ eliminates the xy-term and restores standard form.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Origin-centered layout: thin black x and y axes with arrowheads and italic serif labels x (right) and y (top). Orange rotated axes through the origin at roughly 30–45° counterclockwise, labeled x' (upper right) and y' (upper left), with matching orange arrowheads. Dark blue ellipse outline (no fill) centered at origin, major axis along x', clearly crossing the black x-axis on both sides. Small arc with arrowhead from the positive x-axis to the positive x'-axis, labeled θ in italic. No tick marks or numbers on any axis. Equation display near a corner: the x,y form shows a visible xy-term (e.g. Ax² + Bxy + Cy² + ... = 1) that highlights when active; the x',y' form shows the standard A'x'² + C'y'² = 1, with the active axes brightening together with its equation. Clicked point: small dot on the ellipse with dashed perpendicular projection lines to both axis pairs, orange for x'y', black for xy, and coordinate readout labels.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for rotating the coordinate frame by theta: the learner drags theta, the orange x' and y' axes turn with the ellipse while the black x and y axes stay fixed, showing how rotation removes the visual misalignment behind an xy term.
- Toggle between original and rotated equations: the learner switches from the x,y equation with the xy term to the x',y' equation aligned to the ellipse, and the active axes and equation terms highlight together to show why the rotated frame simplifies the conic.
- Click for coordinate comparison at a point: the learner clicks a point on the ellipse, projections to both axis systems appear with two coordinate readouts, making clear that the same point has different coordinates in the two frames.

authoredContext:
Until now, we have looked at equations of conic sections without an xy term, which aligns the graphs with the x- and y-axes. When we add an xy term, we are rotating the conic about the origin. If the x- and y-axes are rotated through an angle, say θ, then every point on the plane may be thought of as having two representations: (x,y) on the Cartesian plane with the original x-axis and y-axis, and (x ′, y ′) on the new plane defined by the new, rotated axes, called the x'-axis and y'-axis. See the figure.

The graph of the rotated ellipse x 2 + y 2 –xy–15=0

An ellipse centered at the origin, aligned with a rotated coordinate system (x', y') that is at an angle θ with respect to the standard (x, y) coordinate system.

We will find the relationships between x and y on the Cartesian plane with x ′ and y ′ on the new rotated plane. See the figure.

discrepancies: at the default (step-0) state the orange x′/y′ axes are drawn at θ = 30° while the ellipse is tilted 45°, so the rotated axes do not lie along the ellipse's major/minor axes as they clearly do in the source; the source-equivalent configuration only appears after advancing the demo or dragging the slider
the generated ellipse is noticeably more eccentric (semi-axis ratio ≈ 2.1:1) than the source's rounder ellipse (≈ 1.6:1)

the source's θ arc sits between the x-axis and the x′-axis with the axes aligned to the ellipse; here at default the arc measures 30° to a misaligned frame, slightly weakening the 'angle of rotation of the conic' reading
an equation readout panel (x,y / x′,y′ conic coefficients) is added in the lower-left that has no counterpart in the source; it is pedagogically useful but extra chrome
evaluation.notes: All source elements (black x/y axes, orange rotated x′/y′ axes, tilted ellipse, θ arc, axis labels) are present with correct colors and the interactions (θ slider, equation-view toggle, clickable point with dual-frame coordinates, 4-step demo) are rich and conceptually correct; the main flaw is that the default state shows the rotated axes at 30° rather than aligned with the 45°-tilted ellipse as in the source.
action_items: Set the default rotation angle to 45° (or make step 1 use θ = 45°) so the step-0 rendering matches the source figure, with the rotated axes lying along the ellipse's axes; use a 'misaligned' angle only as a later exploratory step.
Adjust the semi-axis ratio (e.g. SEA ≈ 3.0, SEB ≈ 1.9) to better match the rounder ellipse proportions of the source.
Slightly reduce the visual weight of the equation panel (smaller font or collapsible) so it doesn't compete with the figure itself at inline size.

feedback.rationale: Scores are high (4.4 average, concept 5, interactivity 5) with no failure modes; the remaining discrepancies (default 30° vs 45° state, ellipse eccentricity, extra equation panel) are minor polish items that don't undermine the figure's correctness or usability.
